Collapsed, a press on a group that is a destination emits change and leaves the drawer collapsed.

behavior.text: THE navigation drawer SHALL draw a group's chevron where chevron says, as the tree view does. WHILE chevron is start THE navigation drawer SHALL keep a box of comp.navigation-drawer.item.trailing-icon.size.regular at the start of every expanded row's content, comp.navigation-drawer.item.gap before its icon, the icon's room or its label, draw the chevron in it on a group's row and nothing on a destination's, so that the icons and labels of a level each stand in one column, and turn it a quarter turn from pointing toward the end of the line WHILE the group is closed to pointing down WHILE it is open. WHILE chevron is end it SHALL draw expand_more at the very end of the row, after its trailing content, turned half a turn WHILE open. WHILE chevron is none it SHALL draw no chevron and keep no room for one: the arrow keys SHALL still open and close a group (NVD-45); a press on a group's icon SHALL open and close it and choose nothing; WHILE the group is open its icon SHALL be drawn as its openIcon where it has one; a group without an icon SHALL open and close by a press anywhere on its row, unless it is a destination (NVD-66), whose row then chooses it and which the pointer cannot open or close. WHILE the drawer is collapsible THE navigation drawer SHALL draw start as end, so that every icon keeps one point in both forms (NVD-31). WHEN chevron names a value it does not define it SHALL draw start, and in debug builds report the value.
behavior.verify: In `chevron-none` a press on Projects' folder icon opens it and draws folder_open; a press on its label does the same for a group that is not a destination; in `selectable-groups` with chevron none a press on Foundations' label emits change and opens nothing, and Right opens it. In `groups` (chevron start) the labels of every row of a level start on one line.

behavior.text: THE navigation drawer SHALL begin each row's content, and WHILE highlight is indented its item container, one step of indent further from the start than its group's row for each group that holds it, as the tree view does. WHILE indent is null (auto) a step SHALL be what the group's row draws before its label — its start chevron's room and comp.navigation-drawer.item.gap WHILE chevron is start, and its icon (or the icon's room, NVD-71) and comp.navigation-drawer.item.gap — so that a row's first part (its start chevron, its icon or its label) lines up with where its group's label begins, and comp.navigation-drawer.item.nest-indent.regular WHERE the group's row draws neither. WHILE indent is a number a step SHALL be that many units of the layout, and 0 SHALL begin every row where its group's row begins. WHILE the steps of a row's levels would begin its label past half of the drawer's width THE navigation drawer SHALL begin the row so that its label begins there, as the tree view does, so that a deep row keeps room for its name, at 200 % text too. A step SHALL NOT change a row's height, its hit area (NVD-6), which stays the drawer's width, or the collapsed form, which draws no nested row (NVD-32). WHEN indent is negative or not a number THE navigation drawer SHALL draw auto, and in debug builds report the value.
behavior.verify: Test: in `nested-icons` a nested icon starts where its group's label starts (auto); with indent 0 it starts where its group's icon starts; with indent 20 it starts 20 further than its group's. In a drawer of five levels the labels of the third level and below begin at half of the drawer's width.

behavior.text: WHILE highlight is indented THE navigation drawer SHALL draw a nested row's item container — its selected fill, its hover and press layers and its focus indicator — from where the row begins (NVD-69) to the drawer's padding at its end, and WHILE highlight is full from the drawer's padding at its start to its padding at its end at every level, the content starting where the row begins either way; WHEN highlight names a value it does not define it SHALL draw indented, and in debug builds report the value.
behavior.verify: Test: a hovered nested destination's state layer starts where its row begins under indented, and 12 from the drawer's start edge under full.

behavior.text: WHILE iconSpace is auto THE navigation drawer SHALL keep an icon's room, empty, on a row without an icon WHERE another row of its level (the same group's rows, or the drawer's top-level rows) has an icon, so that the labels of the level start on one line; WHILE it is always on every row without an icon; and WHILE it is never on none, the label then starting comp.navigation-drawer.item.padding-inline.regular from where the row's content starts. The room is the icon's box and and counts toward the next level's step (NVD-69).
behavior.verify: In `icon-space` the label of Drafts, which has no icon, starts where Inbox's label does.

behavior.text: WHILE expandable is false THE navigation drawer SHALL draw every group open whatever its open says, draw no chevron and keep no room for one, emit no toggle, and SHALL expose no group as expandable: a group that is a destination (NVD-66) SHALL be that destination alone, and every other group's row SHALL be drawn, take no focus, answer no pointer and be hidden from assistive technology, its label naming the list of its items, which stays a list inside the drawer's list. WHILE the drawer is collapsed it SHALL still draw each top-level group as one cell, whose activation expands the drawer (NVD-47).

behavior.text: WHILE guides is shown THE navigation drawer SHALL draw, for each open group that shows at least one row under it while the drawer is expanded, one line comp.navigation-drawer.guide.width wide in comp.navigation-drawer.guide.color from the lower edge of the group's row to the lower edge of the last row shown under it, centred under the group's first part — its start chevron, else its icon or the icon's room, else at the start of its label — as the tree view does; WHILE guides is hover it SHALL draw the same lines only while the pointer is over the drawer or focus is in it, fading them in and out over comp.navigation-drawer.motion.state-duration with comp.navigation-drawer.motion.state-easing (at once where motion is reduced); WHILE guides is none it SHALL draw none. In forced colors they SHALL be drawn in the system's line color.

behavior.text: WHILE a destination's or a group's supportingText is not empty THE navigation drawer SHALL draw it in comp.navigation-drawer.item.supporting-text.typescale and its condition's supporting-text color (comp.navigation-drawer.unselected.item.supporting-text.color, comp.navigation-drawer.selected.item.supporting-text.color): WHILE supportingPosition is below on a line of its own under the label, the row growing to hold it with comp.navigation-drawer.item.padding-block.regular above and below its text, and WHILE it is inline after the label on its line, comp.navigation-drawer.item.gap after it; it SHALL be one line unless supportingWrap is true (NVD-75), SHALL be read as the row's description after its name and state, and SHALL NOT be drawn while the drawer is collapsed.
behavior.verify: In `supporting`: Inbox's "3 new" stands under its label, comp.navigation-drawer.item.padding-block.regular above the row's lower edge; Drafts' stands after its label on the same line.

behavior.text: WHILE labelWrap is false THE navigation drawer SHALL draw each row's label on one line, cut with an ellipsis at the end of its own direction where it does not fit, and WHILE supportingWrap is false the same for its supporting text, below or inline; WHILE either is true that text SHALL wrap and the row grow with it. THE row's accessible name SHALL be its full label, and its description its full supporting text, whatever is drawn. WHEN a row whose label or supporting text is cut is hovered with a fine pointer, after the tooltip's show delay, or receives keyboard focus, THE navigation drawer SHALL show the full text in a plain tooltip beside the row, toward the content (NVD-56), which Escape dismisses, which stays while the pointer is over the row or focus is on it, and which SHALL NOT be shown for a row whose text is drawn whole.

behavior.text: WHILE an open group's loading is true THE navigation drawer SHALL draw one loading row under it, after the rows of any items it already holds, one step of indent further in (NVD-69): a Loading indicator component of the small size in the place of a row's icon, and after it loadingLabel in comp.navigation-drawer.item.supporting-text.typescale and comp.navigation-drawer.unselected.item.supporting-text.color, in a row of comp.navigation-drawer.item.container.height.regular. It is not a destination: it SHALL take no focus and answer no pointer, SHALL be counted among no items, and SHALL be named by loadingLabel; THE navigation drawer SHALL expose the list of the group's items as busy WHILE loading is true, and announce nothing itself. WHILE loadingLabel is empty it SHALL draw the indicator alone and in debug builds report that the loading row has no name.

behavior.text: WHILE stickyParents is true and the drawer is expanded THE navigation drawer SHALL keep pinned at the top of the space its items scroll in the rows of the open groups that hold the first row shown below the pinned rows, at most stickyMax of them, the innermost winning as VS Code keeps its innermost scopes, one per level and each directly under the one above: each pinned row SHALL be the row itself (no copy is drawn or exposed), keep its own fill, state and focus ring, stay interactive as its row is, be drawn over the rows scrolling under it on comp.navigation-drawer.sticky.container.color (a modal drawer's on its own container color), and leave as its group's last row scrolls past, as the platform's sticky position does; the last pinned row SHALL draw an edge comp.navigation-drawer.sticky.divider.width wide in comp.navigation-drawer.sticky.divider.color at its lower side. WHEN keyboard focus moves to a row hidden under the pinned rows THE navigation drawer SHALL scroll it into view below them (NVD-61's least distance, measured from their lower edge), and bring the selection into view below them (NVD-57). Nothing is animated beyond the scroll itself. WHILE the drawer is collapsed, or stickyParents is false, no row SHALL be pinned. WHEN stickyMax is not a positive whole number it SHALL pin 2, and in debug builds report the value.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on an item's host — a destination's or a group's — THE navigation drawer SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on the element that carries the row's role (its link or its button), in both forms of the drawer — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it, an error message as part of the description while the item is invalid — except those an item owns (aria-current, aria-disabled, and for a group aria-expanded and aria-controls), which it SHALL move and not expose. WHEN the product removes the aria- attribute or its data-aria- twin THE navigation drawer SHALL take it off that element. WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute an item owns THE navigation drawer SHALL report it in debug builds.

keyboard.action: Moves focus through the header's content, then the destinations and group rows that are shown and not disabled, and after the row of a group that is a destination its chevron; inside an open modal drawer it wraps around and never leaves the drawer; from an open standard drawer, expanded or collapsed, it moves on to the content, and the drawer stays as it is.

Activates the focused destination (Enter only for a destination that is a link: it follows the link, and Space is left to the platform), and a modal drawer then closes; on a group's row, opens or closes the group, or, for a group that is a destination (NVD-66), activates it as a destination and leaves it as it is; on that group's chevron, opens or closes the group; on a group's cell in the collapsed drawer, expands the drawer with the group open; on the menu button, changes the drawer's form.

keyboard.action: What the browser does with a link: another tab or window, a download. The drawer emits nothing, selects nothing and stays as it is (NVD-60).

keyboard.action: On a closed group's row, the arrow toward the end of the line opens it; on an open group's row, the arrow toward the start closes it; on an item inside an open group, the arrow toward the start moves focus to the group's row. Elsewhere the keys do nothing.
Closes an open modal drawer (a collapsible one narrows back to its column) and returns focus to where it was.

accessibility.labeling: Each destination is named by its label in both forms, drawn or not, as a button or as a link; its icon is decorative; its badge's description and then its trailing content are part of its description. A group's row and the list of its items are named by the group's label. A section's heading is a heading. The drawer's label names the navigation landmark and, while the drawer is modal and open, the dialog. The menu button is named by its own label and carries the drawer's expanded state; the main action is named by its label in both forms. A collapsed drawer that draws no labels shows each cell's name where the platform shows a name for an icon alone (a tooltip on the web).
notes: The drawer is a list of places, not a tab bar, in both forms: on native platforms its destinations are buttons (or links) with the selected state (as iPadOS sidebars and Android's drawer items are read), and on the web links or buttons with aria-current in a navigation landmark. The collapsed form keeps these semantics; it does not become a tab bar.

Selected and the current page are one thing. The drawer lists the product's places and the selected one is the place being shown, which the web exposes as aria-current="page" on a button and on a link alike. A site of separate pages changes who says which it is — the page, through value, not a press — and nothing else: no destination is ever selected and another current, so a second state would have no case to draw.

A drawer of links is a navigation landmark holding lists of links and disclosure buttons, the pattern assistive technology users know from site navigation: every link and every group's row is its own Tab stop, and the arrow keys only open, close and leave a group. It is deliberately not a choice per use. One Tab stop with roving arrow keys is a tree's or a menu's model, would hide links from the browser's own ways of listing and following them, and would make the same component answer the keyboard in two ways. A long tree is passed by the landmark, by the headings of its sections, by closing its groups, and by the page's skip link.

Showing the selection (NVD-57, NVD-58) scrolls the drawer and opens groups without moving focus and without an announcement: the page's own title and heading say where the user is, and the current destination carries its state for whoever reaches it.

Groups are disclosures, not a tree: a group's row is a button with an expanded state that shows or hides a named list, and every shown destination stays its own tab stop, as the links of a navigation region are. A tree's single tab stop and arrow-key roving would make the drawer's keyboard model depend on whether it has groups; the arrow keys here only open, close and leave a group.

A group that is a destination (selectableGroups, NVD-66) is the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices' disclosure navigation menu with top-level links: its row is the link or button of its own page, with the current-page state, and its chevron a separate disclosure button for its items, each a Tab stop. The two are never one control: a row that both navigates and toggles would announce one action and do two, and a keyboard user could not open the group without leaving the page. The chevron is named by the group's label, as Tanrei ships no words of its own; its role and its expanded state tell it from the row.

Collapsing hides the header slot, the headings' text, trailing content and the items inside groups from assistive technology and focus; it changes no destination's role, name or state, and the menu button announces the change as its expanded state.

A responsive drawer (NVD-53 to NVD-55) changes what it is with the window's width — a layout region where the window is wide, a modal overlay where it is narrow — and each presentation has the semantics of the drawer it stands for. A change of presentation closes an open overlay, releases focus that was kept inside it and announces nothing by itself; the presentation is never the only way to reach a destination, because the product's menu button opens the modal presentation.

The standard form is a layout region, not an overlay, expanded or collapsed: opening it moves focus in, to the selected destination or else the first, closing it returns focus to where it was, and focus leaving it never closes it. The modal form is a modal overlay: it keeps focus in and draws a scrim; a collapsible modal drawer's column is a layout region while the drawer is closed. The web presents the open modal drawer with a modal <dialog> element (showModal gives inertness and Escape); Compose draws it in a window of its own (a Dialog, as TanreiDialog is) and Flutter as a controlled overlay in a Stack over the page, each with a scrim, trapping focus and answering back; SwiftUI, which has no side presentation, overlays it with the modal trait and the escape gesture; React Native presents it in a transparent Modal.
Opening a modal drawer by a swipe from the screen edge is left out: on iOS the same edge is the back gesture. The product opens it from a menu button.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

web.name: tanrei-navigation-drawer
web.notes: Children are `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-item>`, `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-group>` and `<tanrei-navigation-drawer-section>` elements, in order; header buttons (icon-only `<tanrei-button>`s) and the main action (`<tanrei-main-action-button>`) are children with `slot="header-button"` and `slot="main-action"`, and the header slot is `header`. `collapsedLabels` is the `collapsed-labels` attribute; `expanded` is reflected, and so is a read-only `collapsed` state attribute for styling. Modal: a `<dialog>` in the shadow root opened with `showModal()`, its `::backdrop` the scrim; Escape and a press on the backdrop close it, the host sets `open` to false and fires `close`; a collapsible modal drawer keeps its column in the host's layout box and widens the dialog from it. Standard: a `<nav>` named by `label`. The drawer selects the activated destination itself (sets `value`) before firing `change`, sets `expanded` (or `open`) before firing `expandedchange`, and sets a group's `open` before the group fires `toggle`. It sets `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` on its first header button's inner button through the Button's `ariaExpanded` / `ariaControlsElements` element properties, and the Main Action Button's `extended` from its own form. `responsive` is an attribute: the element reads its system's `breakpoint.expanded` and `breakpoint.collapsed` custom properties from its computed style, listens to the two widths with `matchMedia`, exposes the result as the read-only `presentation` property (reflected as a state attribute for styling) and fires `presentationchange` with `detail.presentation`; nothing about the presentation is written to `variant`, `open` or `expanded`, and nothing is kept in storage. Before the element is upgraded, and in the React wrapper on a server, no dialog is open and nothing is inert. A collapsed cell that draws no label shows its name in a plain tooltip. Insets are `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. It lags the spec: it ships an earlier form of the drawer, with a separate rail element beside it. It does not yet follow NVD-57 to NVD-64, nor the parts of NVD-1, NVD-21 and NVD-23 that go with them. `reveal-selected` is an attribute. `scroll-offset` is an attribute read once, for the first frame, and `scrollOffset` a property whose getter returns the scroller's present `scrollTop` and whose setter writes it; the scroller has `overscroll-behavior: contain` and `scroll-behavior: auto`, and bringing the selection into view is a write to `scrollTop`, never `scrollIntoView` (which would also scroll the page). For a link destination `change` and `reselect` are cancelable, carry `detail.href` beside `detail.value`, and are fired from the anchor's `click` only when `event.button` is 0, no modifier key is down, the click was not already cancelled, and the item's `target` is `same` and it has no `download`; cancelling one calls `preventDefault()` on that click. The drawer does not set `value` for a link. Nothing is read from or written to `sessionStorage` or `localStorage`: a site keeps the groups' `open` and `scrollOffset` itself (on `toggle` and on `pagehide`) and writes them back as attributes in the page's markup, or in an inline script placed after the drawer's markup, before the elements are upgraded. `density` is reflected; a value a design system added is read from its own tokens, falling back to regular's. `selectableGroups` is the `selectable-groups` attribute. The attributes are `chevron`, `guides`, `indent` (auto or a number), `highlight`, `icon-space`, `expandable` (`expandable="false"` turns it off), `label-wrap`, `supporting-wrap`, `sticky-parents`, `sticky-max` and `loading-label`; on the items `supporting-text`, `supporting-position`, and on a group `open-icon`, `trailing-text`, `loading` and the `trailing` slot.

destination.name: tanrei-navigation-drawer-item
destination.notes: `icon` is the glyph's name; none, no icon. `short-label`, `trailing-text`, `badge-count` and `badge-label` are attributes; the trailing slot is `trailing`. `badge` is the boolean of the icon badge; a destination's trailing text is `trailing-text`. `href` makes the destination a link: the cell is an `<a href>` in the item's shadow root. `target` is the `target` attribute with the values `same` and `new` (the HTML spellings `_self` and `_blank` are read as those two), `targetLabel` the `target-label` attribute, and `rel` (to which `new` adds `noopener`) and `download` are web-only and forwarded to the anchor, all as `<tanrei-button>`'s. swiftui.notes: `TanreiNavigationDrawer(variant:, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, selection: Binding<Value>, isCollapsible:, isExpanded: Binding<Bool>, collapsedLabelVisibility:, onReselect:) { TanreiNavigationDrawerItem(…); TanreiNavigationDrawerGroup(…) { … }; TanreiNavigationDrawerSection(…) { … } } header: { … } headerButtons: { … } mainAction: { … }`, and for a modal drawer the modifier `.tanreiNavigationDrawer(isPresented:…)` on the content it covers. Not built yet: selectableGroups (NVD-66, NVD-67) — a group that is a destination, with its row choosing it and its chevron a control of its own that opens and closes it. Not built yet: the row model shared with the tree view (chevron, guides, indent, highlight, iconSpace, expandable, labelWrap and supportingWrap, supporting text, one-line labels with a tooltip where cut, a group's trailing content, openIcon and loading row, stickyParents and stickyMax; NVD-68 to NVD-77).
